# Secure Techies

> Secure Techies LLC is a Los Angeles–based managed IT services provider (MSP) and cybersecurity company founded in 2016, headquartered at 21515 Vanowen St Suite 1110, Canoga Park, CA 91303. We provide proactive, security-first technology management, 24/7 support, and rapidly deployable mobile video surveillance for small and mid-size businesses across Los Angeles, the San Fernando Valley, and all of Southern California. Phone: (818) 431-5607. Email: info@SecureTechie.com.

## Services
- [Mobile CCTV Trailers](https://securetechie.com/services/mobile-cctv-trailers/): Solar-powered, rapidly deployable mobile surveillance trailers with HD day/night cameras, 360° coverage, AI analytics, two-way audio, real-time alerts, and live 24/7 remote monitoring. Deploys in under an hour with no power or internet required. Ideal for construction sites, parking lots and dealerships, storage facilities, industrial yards, remote/off-grid sites, and events.
- [Managed Infrastructure](https://securetechie.com/services/infrastructure/): Remote and onsite IT support, infrastructure design, server management, and virtualization with Azure, AWS, and VMware.

## Case Studies
- Hub: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/. Project records: situation, method, outcome. Clients anonymized when required.
- A close call with a fake wire instruction: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/wire-fraud-email-close-call/. Law firm lookalike email, call-back, mailbox review, DMARC path. No invented dollar save.
- Switching IT providers without a weekend outage: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/switching-it-providers/. Five-week parallel MSP handoff for a Valley contractor. Inventory, restore test, then cancel. No planned weekend outage.
- CrowdStrike outage response for a healthcare practice: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/crowdstrike-outage-response/. July 19, 2024 Falcon content update. Safe Mode, BitLocker, rooms first. Not invented percentages.
- IT risk assessment for a Southern California financial firm: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/financial-services-risk-assessment/. Four-week NIST CSF 2.0-aligned assessment, ranked register, 30/60/90 plan. Not a certification.
- Microsoft 365 email migration for a professional services firm: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/microsoft-365-email-migration/
- A backup restore test before tax season: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/backup-restore-test-tax-season/. CPA firm, shared mailbox and SharePoint library restored to a test location. Green jobs were not proof. No invented time-save.
- Microsoft Intune without recalling every laptop: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/microsoft-intune-rollout/. Brokerage. Autopilot, Pro upgrades, app protection on phones, wipe test on a spare. Not full MDM of personal iPhones.
- Guest Wi-Fi that stopped at the register: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/restaurant-guest-wifi-isolation/. Restaurant. Guest VLAN, deny LAN, client isolation, dining-room test. Not a PCI QSA seal.
- A mobile surveillance trailer on a warehouse yard: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/warehouse-mobile-surveillance-trailer/. 3PL. Solar unit on gravel, dusk walk, night test. No invented theft-drop percentage.
- Co-managed IT after the internal admin left: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/co-managed-it-after-admin-left/. Manufacturer. Coordinator stayed. Help desk, Microsoft 365, backups. No PLC work. Not a full outsourcing.
- Microsoft 365 MFA without locking out the board: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/microsoft-365-mfa-rollout/. Nonprofit. Shared finance mailbox, Authenticator, grace window, then enforce. Not FIDO for every volunteer on day one.
- A two-week business firewall cleanup: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/business-firewall-cleanup/. Independent school. Any-any leftover, unused VPN, staff vs student path, weekend test. Not a CIPA seal.
- SharePoint oversharing cleanup for a media agency: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/sharepoint-external-sharing-cleanup/. Anyone links off, stale guests cut, finance vs campaign sliders. Not a DAM.
- Dark web credentials we could actually reset: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/dark-web-credential-alert/. Tech firm. Dump named three work emails. Reset, MFA, stale guest cut, written watch. Not an invented breach count.
- Managed help desk coverage when the office manager was IT: https://securetechie.com/case-studies/help-desk-office-manager/. Small office. Tickets, SSPR, shared mail, joiner path. She stayed operations. Not an invented ticket-time percentage.

## Resources
- Knowledge Center: https://securetechie.com/knowledge-center/
- Blog (IT, cybersecurity, and security guidance): https://securetechie.com/blog/
- Secure Techies vs a typical MSP (comparison table): https://securetechie.com/blog/secure-techies-vs-typical-msp/
- Microsoft 365 Business Premium vs E3: https://securetechie.com/blog/microsoft-365-business-premium-vs-e3/. Under 300 users, start with Business Premium for bundled security (Intune, Entra ID P1, Defender for Business, Defender for Office 365 Plan 1). E3 is for scale, Windows Enterprise, and heavier eDiscovery. A bare E3 seat can drop SMB Defender features unless you add them back.
- Employee offboarding IT checklist: https://securetechie.com/blog/employee-offboarding-it-checklist/. Same day: block sign-in, revoke sessions, check inbox rules. Do not delete the mailbox on day one. Interactive tool: https://securetechie.com/tools/employee-offboarding-checklist/
- Microsoft 365 backup: https://securetechie.com/blog/microsoft-365-backup/. Recycle bin and retention are not a separate restorable copy. Back up mail, shared mailboxes, OneDrive, and SharePoint; run a restore test.
- Cyber insurance requirements for small business: https://securetechie.com/blog/cyber-insurance-requirements-small-business/. Applications ask for MFA, tested backups, EDR, email authentication, and same-day offboarding. Answer from the tenant, not from memory.
- Microsoft Intune for small business: https://securetechie.com/blog/microsoft-intune-small-business/. Business Premium includes Intune Plan 1. Use MDM on company laptops, app protection on personal phones, Autopilot on Windows Pro (not Home).
- Guest Wi-Fi security for offices: https://securetechie.com/blog/guest-wifi-security-office/. A second SSID is not isolation. Guest VLAN, deny LAN, client isolation, WPA3 or a rotated passphrase. Test from the lobby.
- Vendor risk management for small business: https://securetechie.com/blog/vendor-risk-management-small-business/. Inventory who has data or tenant access, tier them, ask for proof (SOC 2, MFA, breach notice), cut access when the contract ends.
- Manual vs automated penetration testing: https://securetechie.com/blog/manual-penetration-testing-vs-automated/. Scanners find known CVEs fast. Manual testing is for logic flaws, API/auth flows, and chained paths. A scan export is not a pen test.
- Security assessments and penetration testing process: https://securetechie.com/blog/security-assessment-penetration-testing-process/. Scope, infrastructure and APIs, scans, then manual tests. Catch holes so the first crisis is a drill.
- How to design cloud infrastructure for data compliance: https://securetechie.com/blog/cloud-infrastructure-data-compliance/. Map data and regulators. GDPR is transfers, not a Frankfurt pin. CCPA is not CA hosting. Region, encrypt, prove, keep backups in-region.
- What is a unified cybersecurity platform: https://securetechie.com/blog/unified-cybersecurity-platform/. A hub for alerts, logs, and cases. Cuts silos and alert fatigue only if someone still owns the queue. Consolidation first, new logo last. We are an MSP, not a platform vendor.
- Security as a big data problem: https://securetechie.com/blog/security-big-data-problem/. Volume, variety, velocity, veracity. Keep identity, email, and endpoint. Do not invent millions of alerts. Diet and an owner beat a data lake.
- Cybersecurity SaaS UI design: https://securetechie.com/blog/cybersecurity-saas-ui-design/. Research, wireframes, iterative tests, then build to spec. We do not ship a SOC product. Buyers should demand a timed isolate-host demo.
- SIEM detection and response (SDR): https://securetechie.com/blog/siem-detection-response-alert-fatigue/. Not a formal standard name. Means SIEM plus detection plus response (SOAR/XDR/MDR). Correlation and a named on-call cut alert fatigue. A dark SIEM is an archive.
- Frequently asked questions (categorized FAQ with schema): https://securetechie.com/faq/
- Privacy policy: https://securetechie.com/privacy-policy/
